And this was one that Senator Cotton, Senator Romney, Senator Manchin, and others have been for. I'm sorry, I shouldn't say Senator Manchin. He said $11, which I think is an interesting number, because if it's $11, you're above the poverty rate for a typical family of four. So I think we can get to a minimum wage increase that makes sense. And my concern is if you raise it too fast and too high, you will lose jobs and those jobs will tend to be younger people who are, as you know, the primary recipients of jobs that are relatively low income and at their minimum wage or somewhat above minimum wage between $7.25 and say $11 an hour. But I think we can get a bipartisan consensus around that. I'm working with a group. There's a group of 10 Republicans and 10 Democrats who meet periodically and we had a meeting last week on this great topic. And most of us, I think, are going to sign up to a minimum wage increase.
